subject.title: fix(azure): responses model aliases route correctly

question: Should a configured provider with a matching endpoint or model row retain ownership of a manifest alias unless an authoritative suppression explicitly redirects that model?
rationale: This is the central semantic choice behind the fix and changes the shared plugin/provider authentication contract beyond the reproduced Azure case; tests can prove consistency but cannot establish the intended ownership policy.

options.title: Confirm the generic precedence
options.body: Approve configured endpoint/model ownership ahead of alias canonicalization while keeping authoritative suppressions and discovered transport metadata intact.

options.title: Require an Azure-only rule
options.body: Limit the ownership exception to azure-openai-responses, avoiding a generic plugin-alias semantic change but introducing provider-specific policy into the resolver.

recommendation.title: Confirm the generic precedence
recommendation.body: Approve configured endpoint/model ownership ahead of alias canonicalization while keeping authoritative suppressions and discovered transport metadata intact.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged manifest model-catalog contract, planner, and alias integration work most directly defines the ownership semantics being changed.
